claims.claim: CSS is a language for writing style sheets, and a style sheet applies to a document.
HTML supplies a page's structure and content while CSS describes how HTML elements should be displayed or presented.
A CSS rule associates a styling instruction with the document content it applies to; declarations state a property and its value.
A property names the visual feature being set and a value selects that feature's setting; a declaration consists of a property and value.
CSS is maintained as an evolving set of specifications rather than one frozen document.
CSS can be placed in a separate stylesheet or associated with an HTML document, allowing presentation rules to be reused across documents.
